subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Dark Web Explained
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Dark Web Explained.

hook.text: The dark web isn't as scary as movies make it. It's just the part of the internet that search engines can't find.

buildup.text: Dark web sites use .onion addresses and require Tor to access. They're not indexed by Google or Bing.

discovery.text: It hosts everything from journalist tip lines and privacy forums to illegal marketplaces and stolen data.

twist.text: The dark web is a tiny fraction of the internet. Most cybercrime actually happens on the regular web.

climax.text: The dark web is a tool — useful for privacy, dangerous for crime, and much smaller than its reputation.

punchline.text: Smaller than you think. Not as scary either.

quiz.question: What is the dark web?
options: The part of the internet not indexed by search engines, accessed through Tor
A separate internet created by hackers
Any website that requires a password to access
